stops.desc: What five common blood tests check.
stops.sub: A peek under the hood: kidneys, liver, sugar, fats, thyroid, and blood cells.
tldr: A few tubes can show trouble before you feel it.
Five tests cover most screening: metabolic panel, cholesterol, A1c, thyroid, CBC.
Not everyone needs every test. Your age and story decide.
One odd number is a clue, not a diagnosis.
Chest pain or trouble breathing is a 911 call, not a lab order.

metabolic-panel.desc: Kidneys, liver, salts, and sugar in one tube.
metabolic-panel.sub: How your filters filter, how your liver works, and whether salt and sugar are steady.
tldr: BMP is the short version. CMP adds liver and protein numbers.
Creatinine and eGFR tell me how your kidneys filter.
Glucose is a snapshot of sugar right now.
A single odd number usually gets a repeat, not a panic.

cholesterol.desc: The fats riding in your blood, and who should check.
cholesterol.sub: Not the enemy. The trouble is too much of the wrong kind for too long.
tldr: LDL is the kind that parks in artery walls.
HDL helps haul extra cholesterol away.
Most adults can check without fasting now.
Numbers are one piece. Blood pressure, smoking, and family history count too.

a1c.sub: A finger-stick is a snapshot. The A1c is the whole photo album.
tldr: A1c shows average sugar over about three months.
Under 5.7% is normal. 5.7 to 6.4% is prediabetes. 6.5% or higher can mean diabetes.
No fasting needed.
Prediabetes is a fork in the road, not a sentence.

thyroid.desc: TSH, the body's thermostat, in plain words.
thyroid.sub: TSH runs backward from what most people expect. Here is why.
tldr: Your brain is the thermostat. Your thyroid is the furnace.
High TSH usually means a slow thyroid.
Low TSH usually means a thyroid running hot.
Some hair and nail vitamins can scramble the result.

cbc.desc: A headcount of your blood cells.
cbc.sub: Three crews: delivery, defense, and repair. Short or crowded tells me where to look.
tldr: Red cells carry oxygen. Low counts can mean anemia.
White cells fight infection.
Platelets help you clot.
Low iron is common and sneaky.

who-and-how-often.desc: A plain schedule by age and risk.
who-and-how-often.sub: There is no single lab menu. A healthy 25-year-old and a 55-year-old need different things.
tldr: Most adults need fewer labs than they think.
Long-term conditions change the schedule.
Symptoms point to the right test.
More tests can mean more false alarms.

reading-results.desc: What H and L flags really mean.
reading-results.sub: A wall of red H and L flags looks scary. Most of the time it is less dramatic.
tldr: A reference range covers about 95% of healthy people.
So 1 in 20 healthy people land just outside it.
Trends matter more than one number.
A lab calling about a critical result means act now.
